newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier in line with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier in line with JGBs.

text.p: The key June three-month deposit rate contract ended easier on Tuesday, in line with the bearish Japanese government bond (JGB) market.
The June ended the day session at 99.26, after moving in a range of 99.23 to 99.28.
After the close, the Trade Ministry said that Japan's industrial production in September increased a preliminary 1.0 percent from the previous month.
The Trade Ministry also said that it forecasts manufacturers' output to rise four percent in October month-on-month.
The stronger-than-expected September output data depressed JGBs in late trading and the Euroyen June contract in the night session, traders said.
The key overnight call rate was most heavily traded at 0.49 percent, up from Monday's 0.48 percent. The rise reflected fund demand towards the end of the month, traders said.
About 135 billion yen worth of the key three month certificates of deposit was issued at 0.51 percent.
The key CDs were also traded at 0.51 percent on Monday.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market where it had a projected a shortfall of 390 billion yen.
The two-year interest rate swap rate was quoted at 0.92/0.96 percent, up from 0.87/0.91 percent in late Monday trading.
Many market traders said that the BOJ is unlikely to tighten its credit grip until the end of the current fiscal year in March.
